basis: Whole-sign/classical horary per Lilly: Jupiter, lord of the 5th and significator of the son, is placed in the Ascendant (the querent's angle/house), tying the son to the mother's house rather than to a master's household; the Moon in 27 Pisces applies by sextile to Saturn, lord of the 4th (the mother's dwelling), further applying the matter to the home. Venus, lady of the Ascendant in the 9th, describes the mother herself away on a journey (she asked at Lilly's country house), which is why she does not already know he is at home. The Venus-Jupiter trine perfecting 25 July 2 p.m. gives the reunion at home. No testimony places the son's significator with a master figure.
prediction_text: The son is at his mother's own house, not with his master. He is alive and well there, and the mother will meet/find him at home when she returns. (Here 'positive' affirms the second limb of the question as put: at her own house.)
timing: Mother and son meet on 25 July 1638 at 2 p.m., when the significators of mother (Venus) and son (Jupiter) perfect their trine, as computed from the ephemeris in the figure.
